```swift
// Generated by SwiftMockito from Client. Do not edit.
import Foundation
import SwiftMockito

final class MockClient: Mock, Client, @unchecked Sendable {
    init(fileID: String = #fileID, filePath: StaticString = #filePath, line: UInt = #line, column: UInt = #column) {
        super.init(name: "MockClient", site: CallSite(fileID: fileID, filePath: filePath, line: line, column: column))
    }

    var token: String {
        get {
            if let capture = Capture.current {
                capture.record(runtime, "token", key: [])
                return Dummies.resolve(String.self, for: "MockClient.token")
            }
            return runtime.invoke("token", key: [])
        }
        set {
            if let capture = Capture.current {
                capture.record(runtime, "token=", key: [arg(newValue)], args: newValue)
                return
            }
            return runtime.invoke("token=", key: [arg(newValue)], args: newValue)
        }
    }

    var currentUser: User {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "currentUser", key: [])
            return Dummies.resolve(User.self, for: "MockClient.currentUser", fallback: Self._dummyUser)
        }
        return runtime.invoke("currentUser", key: [])
    }

    func cached(id: String) -> User? {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "cached(id:)", key: [arg(id)], args: id)
            return Dummies.resolve(User?.self, for: "MockClient.cached(id:)")
        }
        return runtime.invoke("cached(id:)", key: [arg(id)], args: id)
    }

    nonisolated(nonsending) func fetch(id: String) async throws -> User {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "fetch(id:)", key: [arg(id)], args: id, effects: [.async, .throwing])
            if Capture.continuesAfterRecord, let placeholder = Dummies.placeholder(User.self, fallback: Self._dummyUser) { return placeholder }
            throw CaptureSignal()
        }
        return try await runtime.invokeThrowing("fetch(id:)", key: [arg(id)], args: id)
    }

    func save(_ user: User) throws {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "save(_:)", key: [arg(user)], args: user, effects: .throwing)
            if Capture.continuesAfterRecord { return }
            throw CaptureSignal()
        }
        return try runtime.invokeThrowing("save(_:)", key: [arg(user)], args: user)
    }

    func load(id: String, completion: @escaping (Result<User, Error>) -> Void) {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "load(id:completion:)", key: [arg(id)], args: id, completion)
            return
        }
        return runtime.invoke("load(id:completion:)", key: [arg(id)], args: id, completion)
    }

    private static func _dummyUser() -> User {
        User(id: Dummies.resolve(String.self, for: "User.id"), name: Dummies.resolve(String.self, for: "User.name"))
    }
}
```

```swift
        }
        set {

                capture.record(runtime, "subscript(_:)=", key: [arg(index), arg(newValue)], args: index, newValue)
                return
            }
            return runtime.invoke("subscript(_:)=", key: [arg(index), arg(newValue)], args: index, newValue)
        }
    }

    func item(id: Int) -> String {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "item(id:) (Int) -> String", key: [arg(id)], args: id)
            return Dummies.resolve(String.self, for: "MockCatalog.item(id:) (Int) -> String")

            return Dummies.resolve(String.self, for: "MockCatalog.item(id:) (String) -> String")
        }
        return runtime.invoke("item(id:) (String) -> String", key: [arg(id)], args: id)

            if Capture.continuesAfterRecord, let placeholder = Dummies.placeholder(T.self) { return placeholder }
            throw CaptureSignal()
        }
        return try runtime.invokeThrowing("decode(_:as:)", key: [arg(type: T.self), arg(data), arg(type: type)], args: data, type)
    }

        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "store(_:)", key: [arg(type: T.self), arg(value)], args: value)
            return

        }
```

```swift
import Testing
@testable import SwiftMockito

@Suite struct ClientAcceptanceTests {
    let client = MockClient()
    var sut: UserRepository { UserRepository(client: client) }

    @Test func returnsCachedUserWithoutNetwork() async throws {
        when(client.cached(id: "42")).thenReturn(.fixture)

        let user = try await sut.user(id: "42")

        #expect(user == .fixture)
        verify(client.cached(id: "42")).called(1)
        verifyNoMoreInteractions(client)
    }

    @Test func doesNotSaveWhenFetchFails() async {
        when(client.cached(id: "42")).thenReturn(nil)
        when { try await client.fetch(id: "42") }.thenThrow(ClientError.offline)

        await #expect(throws: ClientError.offline) { try await sut.user(id: "42") }
        verifyNever { try client.save(.fixture) }
    }

    @Test func legacyLoadDeliversUser() async throws {
        when(client.load(id: "42", completion: { _ in }))
            .thenAnswer { (id: String, completion: @escaping (Result<User, Error>) -> Void) in
                completion(.success(User(id: id, name: "Gytis")))
            }

        let user = try await sut.legacyUser(id: "42")

        #expect(user.id == "42")
    }

    @Test func fetchesAndSavesInOrder() async throws {
        when(client.cached(id: "42")).thenReturn(nil)
        when { try await client.fetch(id: "42") }.thenReturn(.fixture)

        _ = try await sut.user(id: "42")

        await verifyInOrder {
            client.cached(id: "42")
            try await client.fetch(id: "42")
            try client.save(.fixture)
        }
        verifyNoMoreInteractions(client)
    }

    @Test func sequentialReturns() {
        when(client.cached(id: "42")).thenReturn(nil, .fixture)
        #expect(client.cached(id: "42") == nil)
        #expect(client.cached(id: "42") == .fixture)
        #expect(client.cached(id: "42") == .fixture)
    }

    @Test func propertyGetterAndSetter() {
        when(client.currentUser).thenReturn(.fixture)
        when(client.token).thenReturn("t")
        client.token = "new"
        #expect(client.currentUser == .fixture)
        #expect(client.token == "t")
        verify { client.token = "new" }.called(1)
        verify(client.token).called(1)
    }

    @Test func missingStubOnThrowingMemberThrows() async {
        await #expect(throws: MissingStubError.self) { try await client.fetch(id: "1") }
    }

    @Test func unstubbedVoidMemberReturns() {
        client.load(id: "1") { _ in Issue.record("completion must not run") }
        verify(client.load(id: "1", completion: { _ in })).called(1)
    }

    @Test func resetForgetsEverything() {
        when(client.cached(id: "1")).thenReturn(.fixture)
        _ = client.cached(id: "1")
        reset(client)
        verifyNever(client.cached(id: "1"))
    }

    @Test func dummiesNeverReachCodeUnderTest() {
        // Recording `currentUser` builds a dummy User; the real call returns the stub.
        when(client.currentUser).thenReturn(User(id: "real", name: "Real"))
        #expect(client.currentUser.id == "real")
    }

    @Test func unstubbedNonThrowingValueTraps() async {
        await #expect(processExitsWith: .failure) {
            _ = MockClient().cached(id: "1")
        }
    }
}
```

The answer closure is annotated (resolved D2): the compiler cannot infer `completion`'s type from the body. Single-parameter answers such as `thenAnswer { id in User(id: id, name: "x") }` infer fine.

```swift
import Foundation
import Testing
@testable import SwiftMockito

@Suite struct CatalogAcceptanceTests {
    let catalog = MockCatalog()

    @Test func subscriptGetAndSet() {
        when(catalog[1]).thenReturn("one")
        catalog[2] = "two"
        #expect(catalog[1] == "one")
        verify { catalog[2] = "two" }.called(1)
    }

    @Test func overloadsAreSeparateMembers() {
        when(catalog.item(id: 1)).thenReturn("int")
        when(catalog.item(id: "1")).thenReturn("string")
        #expect(catalog.item(id: 1) == "int")
        #expect(catalog.item(id: "1") == "string")
    }

    @Test func genericTypeIsPartOfTheKey() throws {
        when { try catalog.decode(Data(), as: Int.self) }.thenReturn(7)
        when { try catalog.decode(Data(), as: String.self) }.thenReturn("seven")
        #expect(try catalog.decode(Data(), as: Int.self) == 7)
        #expect(try catalog.decode(Data(), as: String.self) == "seven")
        catalog.store(1)
        verifyNever(catalog.store(Int64(1)))
        verify(catalog.store(1)).called(1)
    }

    @Test func classArgumentsMatchByIdentity() {
        let a = Reference(), b = Reference()
        when(catalog.describe(a)).thenReturn("a")
        #expect(catalog.describe(a) == "a")
        verifyNever(catalog.describe(b))
    }

    @Test func tupleArgumentsMatchByValue() {
        catalog.tag((1, "x"))
        verify(catalog.tag((1, "x"))).called(1)
    }

    @Test func optionalClosureIsLeftOutOfTheKey() {
        catalog.notify(nil)
        verify(catalog.notify({})).called(1)
    }
}
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing from the runtime (the generator only reads source text).
- Produces:
  - `public struct SourceInput: Sendable { path, module, text }`
  - `public struct GeneratorDiagnostic: Sendable, Equatable, CustomStringConvertible` with `severity` (`.warning` or `.error`), `message`, `path`, `line`, and `column`. `description` is `path:line:column: warning: message`, the format Xcode and SwiftPM surface. Internal factories: `.error(_:at:)` and `.warning(_:at:)`, both taking a `Marker`.

  - `enum Member { case method(Method); case property(Property); case subscriptMember(Subscript) }`. The payloads are `Method { name, identity, genericParameters: [GenericParameter], parameters: [Parameter], returnType: String?, isAsync, isThrowing, genericWhereClause: String?; baseIdentity; signature }`, `Parameter { label: String?, name, type, isClosure, isMetatype, isTuple }`, `Property { name, type, hasSetter, getterAsync, getterThrows }`, and `Subscript { parameters, returnType, hasSetter; identity }`.

`Sources/SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore/Diagnostics.swift`:

```swift
public struct GeneratorDiagnostic: Sendable, Equatable, CustomStringConvertible {
    public enum Severity: String, Sendable { case warning, error }

    public let severity: Severity
    public let message: String
    public let path: String
    public let line: Int
    public let column: Int

    public init(severity: Severity, message: String, path: String, line: Int, column: Int) {
        self.severity = severity
        self.message = message
        self.path = path
        self.line = line
        self.column = column
    }

    public var description: String { "\(path):\(line):\(column): \(severity.rawValue): \(message)" }

    static func error(_ message: String, at marker: Marker) -> Self {
        .init(severity: .error, message: message, path: marker.path, line: marker.line, column: marker.column)
    }

    static func warning(_ message: String, at marker: Marker) -> Self {
        .init(severity: .warning, message: message, path: marker.path, line: marker.line, column: marker.column)
    }
}
```

`Sources/SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore/Model.swift`:

```swift
public struct SourceInput: Sendable {
    public let path: String
    public let module: String
    public let text: String

    public init(path: String, module: String, text: String) {
        self.path = path
        self.module = module
        self.text = text
    }
}

struct Marker: Equatable {
    let protocolName: String
    let path: String
    let line: Int
    let column: Int
}

struct GenericParameter: Equatable {
    let name: String
    let constraint: String?
}

struct Parameter: Equatable {
    let label: String?        // external label; nil means `_` (or no label, for subscripts)
    let name: String          // internal name used in the body
    let type: String          // as written in the protocol
    let isClosure: Bool
    let isMetatype: Bool
    let isTuple: Bool
}

struct Method: Equatable {
    let name: String
    var identity: String
    let genericParameters: [GenericParameter]
    let parameters: [Parameter]
    let returnType: String?   // nil means Void
    let isAsync: Bool
    let isThrowing: Bool
    let genericWhereClause: String?

    var baseIdentity: String { "\(name)(\(parameters.map { "\($0.label ?? "_"):" }.joined()))" }
    var signature: String { "(\(parameters.map(\.type).joined(separator: ", "))) -> \(returnType ?? "Void")" }
}

struct Property: Equatable {
    let name: String
    let type: String
    let hasSetter: Bool
    let getterAsync: Bool
    let getterThrows: Bool
}

struct Subscript: Equatable {
    let parameters: [Parameter]
    let returnType: String
    let hasSetter: Bool

    var identity: String { "subscript(\(parameters.map { "\($0.label ?? "_"):" }.joined()))" }
}

enum Member: Equatable {
    case method(Method)
    case property(Property)
    case subscriptMember(Subscript)
}

struct MockModel {
    let protocolName: String
    let mockName: String
    let access: String
    let globalActor: String?
    let module: String
    let imports: [String]
    let members: [Member]
    let marker: Marker
}
```

`Sources/SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore/SourceIndex.swift`:

```swift
import SwiftParser
import SwiftSyntax

struct IndexedDecl<Node: SyntaxProtocol> {
    let node: Node
    let input: SourceInput
}

enum IndexedType {
    case structDecl(IndexedDecl<StructDeclSyntax>)
    case enumDecl(IndexedDecl<EnumDeclSyntax>)
    case classDecl(IndexedDecl<ClassDeclSyntax>)
    case protocolDecl(IndexedDecl<ProtocolDeclSyntax>)
}

final class SourceIndex {
    private var trees: [(input: SourceInput, tree: SourceFileSyntax)] = []
    private var protocols: [String: IndexedDecl<ProtocolDeclSyntax>] = [:]
    private var types: [String: IndexedType] = [:]
    private var typealiases: [String: TypeSyntax] = [:]

    init(_ inputs: [SourceInput]) {
        for input in inputs {
            let tree = Parser.parse(source: input.text)
            trees.append((input, tree))
            // Top-level declarations only; nested types are out of scope for v1.
            for item in tree.statements {
                guard let decl = item.item.as(DeclSyntax.self) else { continue }
                if let p = decl.as(ProtocolDeclSyntax.self) {
                    let indexed = IndexedDecl(node: p, input: input)
                    protocols[p.name.text] = indexed
                    types[p.name.text] = .protocolDecl(indexed)
                } else if let s = decl.as(StructDeclSyntax.self) {
                    types[s.name.text] = .structDecl(IndexedDecl(node: s, input: input))
                } else if let e = decl.as(EnumDeclSyntax.self) {
                    types[e.name.text] = .enumDecl(IndexedDecl(node: e, input: input))
                } else if let c = decl.as(ClassDeclSyntax.self) {
                    types[c.name.text] = .classDecl(IndexedDecl(node: c, input: input))
                } else if let t = decl.as(TypeAliasDeclSyntax.self) {
                    typealiases[t.name.text] = t.initializer.value
                }
            }
        }
    }

    func markers(in paths: Set<String>) -> [Marker] {
        var result: [Marker] = []
        for (input, tree) in trees where paths.contains(input.path) {
            let converter = SourceLocationConverter(fileName: input.path, tree: tree)
            let visitor = MarkerVisitor(viewMode: .sourceAccurate)
            visitor.walk(tree)
            for attribute in visitor.attributes {
                let location = attribute.startLocation(converter: converter)
                for name in markedTypeNames(attribute) {
                    result.append(Marker(protocolName: name, path: input.path, line: location.line, column: location.column))
                }
            }
        }
        return result
    }

    func protocolDecl(named name: String) -> IndexedDecl<ProtocolDeclSyntax>? { protocols[name] }
    func typeDecl(named name: String) -> IndexedType? { types[name] }
    func typealiasTarget(named name: String) -> TypeSyntax? { typealiases[name] }

    func imports(inFile path: String) -> [String] {
        guard let tree = trees.first(where: { $0.input.path == path })?.tree else { return [] }
        return tree.statements.compactMap { $0.item.as(ImportDeclSyntax.self)?.trimmedDescription }
    }

    private func markedTypeNames(_ attribute: AttributeSyntax) -> [String] {
        guard case .argumentList(let arguments)? = attribute.arguments else { return [] }
        return arguments.compactMap { argument in
            guard let access = argument.expression.as(MemberAccessExprSyntax.self),
                  access.declName.baseName.text == "self",
                  let base = access.base else { return nil }
            return base.trimmedDescription
        }
    }
}

private final class MarkerVisitor: SyntaxVisitor {
    var attributes: [AttributeSyntax] = []

    override func visit(_ node: AttributeSyntax) -> SyntaxVisitorContinueKind {
        if node.attributeName.trimmedDescription == "GenerateMock" { attributes.append(node) }
        return .skipChildren
    }
}
```

`Sources/SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore/ProtocolResolver.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import SwiftSyntax

struct ProtocolResolver {
    let index: SourceIndex

    /// Names of `Mock` members that a protocol requirement must not reuse.
    static let reservedNames: Set<String> = ["runtime"]
    /// Inherited protocols that add no requirements for the mock to implement.
    static let markerProtocols: Set<String> = ["Sendable", "AnyObject", "SendableMetatype"]

    func resolve(_ marker: Marker, testModule: String) -> Result<MockModel, [GeneratorDiagnostic]> {
        guard let root = index.protocolDecl(named: marker.protocolName) else {
            return .failure([.error("\(marker.protocolName): protocol not found in the test target or its dependencies (protocols from binary frameworks are not supported)", at: marker)])
        }
        var files: [String] = []
        let members: [Member]
        switch collect(root, marker: marker, files: &files) {
        case .success(let collected): members = collected
        case .failure(let diagnostics): return .failure(diagnostics)
        }

        let isPublic = root.node.modifiers.contains { ["public", "package"].contains($0.name.text) }
        var plain = Set(files.flatMap { index.imports(inFile: $0) }.filter { !$0.hasSuffix("SwiftMockito") })
        plain.insert("import SwiftMockito")
        var imports = plain.sorted()
        if root.input.module != testModule {
            imports.append(isPublic ? "import \(root.input.module)" : "@testable import \(root.input.module)")
        }
        return .success(MockModel(
            protocolName: marker.protocolName,
            mockName: "Mock\(marker.protocolName)",
            access: isPublic ? "public " : "",
            globalActor: globalActor(of: root.node),
            module: root.input.module,
            imports: imports,
            members: disambiguateOverloads(members),
            marker: marker
        ))
    }

    /// The requirements of `decl` and its inherited protocols, inherited ones first.
    func members(of decl: IndexedDecl<ProtocolDeclSyntax>, marker: Marker) -> Result<[Member], [GeneratorDiagnostic]> {
        var files: [String] = []
        return collect(decl, marker: marker, files: &files).map(disambiguateOverloads)
    }

    private func collect(_ root: IndexedDecl<ProtocolDeclSyntax>, marker: Marker, files: inout [String]) -> Result<[Member], [GeneratorDiagnostic]> {
        var members: [Member] = []
        var diagnostics: [GeneratorDiagnostic] = []
        var visited: Set<String> = []

        func visit(_ decl: IndexedDecl<ProtocolDeclSyntax>) {
            let name = decl.node.name.text
            guard visited.insert(name).inserted else { return }
            files.append(decl.input.path)
            for inherited in decl.node.inheritanceClause?.inheritedTypes ?? [] {
                let parent = inherited.type.trimmedDescription
                if parent == "Actor" {
                    diagnostics.append(.error("\(name): Actor-constrained protocols are not supported", at: marker))
                } else if Self.markerProtocols.contains(parent) {
                    continue
                } else if let parentDecl = index.protocolDecl(named: parent) {
                    visit(parentDecl)
                } else {
                    diagnostics.append(.error("\(name): inherited protocol \(parent) not found in sources", at: marker))
                }
            }
            for item in decl.node.memberBlock.members {
                switch convert(item.decl, protocolName: name, marker: marker) {
                case .success(let member): members.append(member)
                case .failure(let diagnostic): diagnostics.append(diagnostic)
                }
            }
        }

        visit(root)
        return diagnostics.isEmpty ? .success(members) : .failure(diagnostics)
    }

    private func convert(_ decl: DeclSyntax, protocolName: String, marker: Marker) -> Result<Member, GeneratorDiagnostic> {
        func unsupported(_ what: String) -> Result<Member, GeneratorDiagnostic> {
            .failure(.error("\(protocolName): \(what) are not supported", at: marker))
        }
        if let modifiers = decl.asProtocol(WithModifiersSyntax.self)?.modifiers,
           modifiers.contains(where: { $0.name.text == "static" || $0.name.text == "class" }) {
            return unsupported("static requirements")
        }
        if decl.is(InitializerDeclSyntax.self) { return unsupported("initializers") }
        if decl.is(AssociatedTypeDeclSyntax.self) { return unsupported("associated types") }
        if decl.trimmedDescription.range(of: #"\bSelf\b"#, options: .regularExpression) != nil {
            return unsupported("Self requirements")
        }

        if let function = decl.as(FunctionDeclSyntax.self) {
            let name = function.name.text
            let effects = function.signature.effectSpecifiers
            if effects?.throwsClause?.type != nil {
                return .failure(.error("\(protocolName).\(name): typed throws is not supported", at: marker))
            }
            if effects?.throwsClause?.throwsSpecifier.text == "rethrows" {
                return .failure(.error("\(protocolName).\(name): rethrows is not supported", at: marker))
            }
            if Self.reservedNames.contains(name) { return collision(protocolName, name, marker) }
            let returnType = function.signature.returnClause?.type.trimmedDescription
            return .success(.method(Method(
                name: name,
                identity: "",
                genericParameters: function.genericParameterClause?.parameters.map {
                    GenericParameter(name: $0.name.text, constraint: $0.inheritedType?.trimmedDescription)
                } ?? [],
                parameters: function.signature.parameterClause.parameters.enumerated().map { position, p in
                    parameter(label: p.firstName.text, secondName: p.secondName?.text, type: p.type, position: position)
                },
                returnType: (returnType == "Void" || returnType == "()") ? nil : returnType,
                isAsync: effects?.asyncSpecifier != nil,
                isThrowing: effects?.throwsClause != nil,
                genericWhereClause: function.genericWhereClause?.trimmedDescription
            )))
        }

        if let variable = decl.as(VariableDeclSyntax.self), let binding = variable.bindings.first,
           let name = binding.pattern.as(IdentifierPatternSyntax.self)?.identifier.text,
           let type = binding.typeAnnotation?.type {
            if Self.reservedNames.contains(name) { return collision(protocolName, name, marker) }
            let accessors = accessorList(binding.accessorBlock)
            let getter = accessors.first { $0.accessorSpecifier.text == "get" }
            return .success(.property(Property(
                name: name,
                type: type.trimmedDescription,
                hasSetter: accessors.contains { $0.accessorSpecifier.text == "set" },
                getterAsync: getter?.effectSpecifiers?.asyncSpecifier != nil,
                getterThrows: getter?.effectSpecifiers?.throwsClause != nil
            )))
        }

        if let sub = decl.as(SubscriptDeclSyntax.self) {
            return .success(.subscriptMember(Subscript(
                // Subscript parameters have no external label unless the name is written twice.
                parameters: sub.parameterClause.parameters.enumerated().map { position, p in
                    parameter(label: p.secondName == nil ? "_" : p.firstName.text,
                              secondName: p.secondName?.text ?? p.firstName.text, type: p.type, position: position)
                },
                returnType: sub.returnClause.type.trimmedDescription,
                hasSetter: accessorList(sub.accessorBlock).contains { $0.accessorSpecifier.text == "set" }
            )))
        }

        return .failure(.error("\(protocolName): unsupported requirement `\(decl.trimmedDescription)`", at: marker))
    }

    private func accessorList(_ block: AccessorBlockSyntax?) -> AccessorDeclListSyntax {
        if case .accessors(let list)? = block?.accessors { return list }
        return []
    }

    private func collision(_ protocolName: String, _ member: String, _ marker: Marker) -> Result<Member, GeneratorDiagnostic> {
        .failure(.error("\(protocolName).\(member) collides with SwiftMockito's Mock.\(member)", at: marker))
    }

    private func parameter(label: String, secondName: String?, type: TypeSyntax, position: Int) -> Parameter {
        let internalName = secondName ?? label
        let resolved = resolveTypealias(type)
        return Parameter(
            label: label == "_" ? nil : label,
            name: internalName == "_" ? "arg\(position)" : internalName,
            type: type.trimmedDescription,
            isClosure: isClosure(resolved),
            isMetatype: resolved.is(MetatypeTypeSyntax.self),
            isTuple: (resolved.as(TupleTypeSyntax.self)?.elements.count ?? 0) > 1
        )
    }

    /// Follows typealiases declared in the sources, and strips attributes such as `@escaping`.
    private func resolveTypealias(_ type: TypeSyntax) -> TypeSyntax {
        var current = type
        for _ in 0..<8 {
            if let attributed = current.as(AttributedTypeSyntax.self) { current = attributed.baseType; continue }
            if let identifier = current.as(IdentifierTypeSyntax.self), identifier.genericArgumentClause == nil,
               let target = index.typealiasTarget(named: identifier.name.text) { current = target; continue }
            break
        }
        return current
    }

    private func isClosure(_ type: TypeSyntax) -> Bool {
        let base = resolveTypealias(type)
        if base.is(FunctionTypeSyntax.self) { return true }
        if let optional = base.as(OptionalTypeSyntax.self) { return isClosure(optional.wrappedType) }
        if let iuo = base.as(ImplicitlyUnwrappedOptionalTypeSyntax.self) { return isClosure(iuo.wrappedType) }
        if let tuple = base.as(TupleTypeSyntax.self), tuple.elements.count == 1, let only = tuple.elements.first {
            return isClosure(only.type)   // `(() -> Void)?` parses as Optional(Tuple(Function))
        }
        return false
    }

    private func globalActor(of decl: ProtocolDeclSyntax) -> String? {
        for case .attribute(let attribute) in decl.attributes {
            let name = attribute.attributeName.trimmedDescription
            if name.hasSuffix("Actor") { return name }
        }
        return nil
    }

    private func disambiguateOverloads(_ members: [Member]) -> [Member] {
        var counts: [String: Int] = [:]
        for case .method(let m) in members { counts[m.baseIdentity, default: 0] += 1 }
        return members.map { member in
            guard case .method(var m) = member else { return member }
            m.identity = counts[m.baseIdentity, default: 0] > 1 ? "\(m.baseIdentity) \(m.signature)" : m.baseIdentity
            return .method(m)
        }
    }
}
```

- Create: `Tests/GeneratorTests/SnapshotTests.swift`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the Task 12 model, plus the Task 11 goldens (`MockClient`, `MockCatalog`, `MockScreen`, `MockFeed`), read from `Tests/SwiftMockitoTests/Fixtures/` relative to `#filePath`. `MockFeed` is the contract for `public` access, async and throwing property getters (`get async` / `get throws` blocks), async methods with and without a value, and a generic value-returning member.
- Produces:
  - `public struct GeneratorConfiguration { markedPaths: [String]; inputs: [SourceInput]; testModule: String; outputDirectory: String; expectedFiles: [String] = [] }`
  - `public struct GeneratorResult { files: [String: String] /* file name → contents */; diagnostics: [GeneratorDiagnostic]; var hasErrors: Bool }`
  - `public enum Generator { static func generate(_:) -> GeneratorResult; static func run(arguments: [String]) -> Int32 }`. `run` parses CLI arguments, reads files, writes outputs (skipping files whose contents are unchanged), prints diagnostics to stderr, and returns 0 on success, 1 on generation errors, or 2 on usage errors.
  - CLI: `SwiftMockitoGenerator generate --test-module <M> --output <dir> --marked <file>... [--source <Module>=<file>...] [--source-dir <Module>=<dir>...] [--expect <MockP.swift>...]`. Every name passed with `--expect` is always written: a mock, an `#error(...)` file when generation failed, or a comment-only file when the parser found no such marker. Build systems that declared the file therefore never miss an output.
  - `final class DummySynthesizer { init(index:model:); func fallback(for type: String, member: String, genericNames: Set<String>, warn: Bool = true) -> String?; var helpers: [String]; var warnings: [GeneratorDiagnostic] }`
  - `struct MockEmitter { init(model:synthesizer:); func emit() -> String }`

```swift
import Foundation
import Testing
@testable import SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore

/// `Tests/SwiftMockitoTests/Fixtures`, which holds the compiled goldens.
let fixtures = URL(filePath: #filePath).deletingLastPathComponent()
    .deletingLastPathComponent().appending(path: "SwiftMockitoTests/Fixtures")

/// Every fixture protocol file that exists so far (Store arrives in Task 14).
func fixtureInputs() -> [SourceInput] {
    ["Client.swift", "Catalog.swift", "Screen.swift", "Feed.swift", "Store.swift"].compactMap { name in
        let url = fixtures.appending(path: name)
        guard let text = try? String(contentsOf: url, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
        return SourceInput(path: url.path, module: "SwiftMockitoTests", text: text)
    }
}

func generate(marking names: [String], module: String = "SwiftMockitoTests") -> GeneratorResult {
    let marker = SourceInput(path: "/virtual/Mocks.swift", module: module,
                             text: "@GenerateMock(\(names.map { "\($0).self" }.joined(separator: ", ")))\nenum Mocks {}\n")
    return Generator.generate(GeneratorConfiguration(
        markedPaths: [marker.path], inputs: [marker] + fixtureInputs(),
        testModule: module, outputDirectory: "/unused"))
}

@Suite struct SnapshotTests {
    @Test(arguments: ["Client", "Catalog", "Screen", "Feed"])
    func generatorReproducesGolden(protocolName: String) throws {
        let result = generate(marking: [protocolName])
        #expect(result.diagnostics.isEmpty)
        let expected = try String(contentsOf: fixtures.appending(path: "Mock\(protocolName).swift"), encoding: .utf8)
        let actual = try #require(result.files["Mock\(protocolName).swift"])
        #expect(actual == expected, "\(firstDifference(actual, expected))")
    }

    @Test func outputIsDeterministic() {
        #expect(generate(marking: ["Catalog", "Client"]).files == generate(marking: ["Catalog", "Client"]).files)
    }

    @Test func duplicateMockNamesCollide() {
        let marker = SourceInput(path: "/v/M.swift", module: "T", text: "@GenerateMock(Client.self)\nenum A {}\n@GenerateMock(Client.self)\nenum B {}\n")
        let result = Generator.generate(GeneratorConfiguration(markedPaths: [marker.path],
            inputs: [marker] + fixtureInputs(), testModule: "T", outputDirectory: "/unused"))
        #expect(result.diagnostics == [GeneratorDiagnostic(severity: .error,
            message: "MockClient is generated twice; remove the duplicate @GenerateMock(Client.self)",
            path: "/v/M.swift", line: 3, column: 1)])
    }

    @Test func failedProtocolStillWritesAnErrorFile() {
        let result = generate(marking: ["Missing"])
        #expect(result.hasErrors)
        #expect(result.files["MockMissing.swift"]?.contains("#error(") == true)
    }

    @Test func expectedButUnmarkedFileIsWrittenEmpty() {
        let marker = SourceInput(path: "/v/M.swift", module: "T", text: "// @GenerateMock(Client.self)\n")
        let result = Generator.generate(GeneratorConfiguration(markedPaths: [marker.path], inputs: [marker],
            testModule: "T", outputDirectory: "/unused", expectedFiles: ["MockClient.swift"]))
        #expect(result.files == ["MockClient.swift": "// Generated by SwiftMockito. No active @GenerateMock(Client.self) found.\n"])
        #expect(result.diagnostics.isEmpty)
    }
}

func firstDifference(_ a: String, _ b: String) -> String {
    let al = a.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)
    let bl = b.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)
    for i in 0..<max(al.count, bl.count) where i >= al.count || i >= bl.count || al[i] != bl[i] {
        return "line \(i + 1):\n  generated: \(i < al.count ? String(al[i]) : "<eof>")\n  golden:    \(i < bl.count ? String(bl[i]) : "<eof>")"
    }
    return "identical"
}
```

```swift
        let dir = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appending(path: UUID().uuidString)
        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: dir, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
        let marked = dir.appending(path: "Mocks.swift")

        let out = dir.appending(path: "out")

        let code = Generator.run(arguments: [

            "--source", "SwiftMockitoTests=\(fixtures.appending(path: "Client.swift").path)",
        ])

        #expect(code == 0)
        let written = try String(contentsOf: out.appending(path: "MockClient.swift"), encoding: .utf8)
```

`Sources/SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore/CodeWriter.swift`:

```swift
struct CodeWriter {
    private(set) var output = ""
    private var level = 0

    mutating func line(_ text: String = "") {
        output += text.isEmpty ? "\n" : String(repeating: "    ", count: level) + text + "\n"
    }

    mutating func lines(_ text: String) {
        text.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).forEach { line(String($0)) }
    }

    mutating func block(_ opener: String, _ body: (inout CodeWriter) -> Void) {
        line(opener + " {")
        level += 1
        body(&self)
        level -= 1
        line("}")
    }
}
```

```swift
struct MockEmitter {
    let model: MockModel
    let synthesizer: DummySynthesizer

    func emit() -> String {
        // Members first: emitting them tells the synthesizer which helpers are needed.
        var body = CodeWriter()
        for member in model.members {
            body.line()
            switch member {
            case .method(let m): emitMethod(m, &body)
            case .property(let p): emitProperty(p, &body)
            case .subscriptMember(let s): emitSubscript(s, &body)
            }
        }
        for helper in synthesizer.helpers {
            body.line()
            body.lines(helper)
        }

        var w = CodeWriter()
        w.line("// Generated by SwiftMockito from \(model.protocolName). Do not edit.")
        model.imports.forEach { w.line($0) }
        w.line()
        if let actor = model.globalActor { w.line("@\(actor)") }
        w.block("\(model.access)final class \(model.mockName): Mock, \(model.protocolName), @unchecked Sendable") { w in
            w.block("\(model.access)init(fileID: String = #fileID, filePath: StaticString = #filePath, line: UInt = #line, column: UInt = #column)") { w in
                w.line("super.init(name: \"\(model.mockName)\", site: CallSite(fileID: fileID, filePath: filePath, line: line, column: column))")
            }
            w.lines(String(body.output.dropLast()).indented())
        }
        return w.output
    }

    // MARK: Members

    private func emitMethod(_ m: Method, _ w: inout CodeWriter) {
        let generics = m.genericParameters.isEmpty ? "" : "<" + m.genericParameters.map { p in
            p.constraint.map { "\(p.name): \($0)" } ?? p.name
        }.joined(separator: ", ") + ">"
        let params = m.parameters.map { declaration($0, subscriptStyle: false) }.joined(separator: ", ")
        let effects = (m.isAsync ? " async" : "") + (m.isThrowing ? " throws" : "")
        let returns = m.returnType.map { " -> \($0)" } ?? ""
        let whereClause = m.genericWhereClause.map { " \($0)" } ?? ""
        let key = keyList(genericTypes: m.genericParameters.map(\.name), parameters: m.parameters)
        w.block("\(model.access)\(nonsending(m.isAsync))func \(m.name)\(generics)(\(params))\(effects)\(returns)\(whereClause)") { w in
            emitBody(identity: m.identity, key: key, args: argsList(m.parameters.map(\.name)),
                     isAsync: m.isAsync, isThrowing: m.isThrowing, returnType: m.returnType,
                     genericNames: Set(m.genericParameters.map(\.name)), &w)
        }
    }

    private func emitProperty(_ p: Property, _ w: inout CodeWriter) {
        let getterEffects = (p.getterAsync ? " async" : "") + (p.getterThrows ? " throws" : "")
        w.block("\(model.access)\(nonsending(p.getterAsync))var \(p.name): \(p.type)") { w in
            guard p.hasSetter || !getterEffects.isEmpty else {
                emitBody(identity: p.name, key: "[]", args: "", isAsync: false, isThrowing: false,
                         returnType: p.type, genericNames: [], &w)
                return
            }
            w.block("get\(getterEffects)") { w in
                emitBody(identity: p.name, key: "[]", args: "", isAsync: p.getterAsync, isThrowing: p.getterThrows,
                         returnType: p.type, genericNames: [], &w)
            }
            if p.hasSetter {
                w.block("set") { w in
                    emitBody(identity: "\(p.name)=", key: "[arg(newValue)]", args: ", args: newValue",
                             isAsync: false, isThrowing: false, returnType: nil, genericNames: [], &w)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func emitSubscript(_ s: Subscript, _ w: inout CodeWriter) {
        let params = s.parameters.map { declaration($0, subscriptStyle: true) }.joined(separator: ", ")
        let key = keyList(genericTypes: [], parameters: s.parameters)
        let names = s.parameters.map(\.name)
        w.block("\(model.access)subscript(\(params)) -> \(s.returnType)") { w in
            guard s.hasSetter else {
                emitBody(identity: s.identity, key: key, args: argsList(names), isAsync: false, isThrowing: false,
                         returnType: s.returnType, genericNames: [], &w)
                return
            }
            w.block("get") { w in
                emitBody(identity: s.identity, key: key, args: argsList(names), isAsync: false, isThrowing: false,
                         returnType: s.returnType, genericNames: [], &w)
            }
            w.block("set") { w in
                let setKey = key == "[]" ? "[arg(newValue)]" : String(key.dropLast()) + ", arg(newValue)]"
                emitBody(identity: "\(s.identity)=", key: setKey, args: argsList(names + ["newValue"]),
                         isAsync: false, isThrowing: false, returnType: nil, genericNames: [], &w)
            }
        }
    }

    // MARK: Body

    private func emitBody(identity: String, key: String, args: String, isAsync: Bool, isThrowing: Bool,
                          returnType: String?, genericNames: Set<String>, _ w: inout CodeWriter) {
        let effects: String = switch (isAsync, isThrowing) {
        case (true, true): ", effects: [.async, .throwing]"
        case (true, false): ", effects: .async"
        case (false, true): ", effects: .throwing"
        case (false, false): ""
        }
        let member = "\(model.mockName).\(identity)"
        w.block("if let capture = Capture.current") { w in
            w.line("capture.record(runtime, \"\(identity)\", key: \(key)\(args)\(effects))")
            if isThrowing {
                // Resolved D5: inside verifyInOrder, return a placeholder instead of throwing.
                if let returnType {
                    let fallback = genericNames.contains(returnType) ? nil
                        : synthesizer.fallback(for: returnType, member: member, genericNames: genericNames, warn: false)
                    w.line("if Capture.continuesAfterRecord, let placeholder = Dummies.placeholder(\(metatype(returnType))\(fallback.map { ", fallback: \($0)" } ?? "")) { return placeholder }")
                } else {
                    w.line("if Capture.continuesAfterRecord { return }")
                }
                w.line("throw CaptureSignal()")
            } else if let returnType {
                let fallback = synthesizer.fallback(for: returnType, member: member, genericNames: genericNames)
                    .map { ", fallback: \($0)" } ?? ""
                w.line("return Dummies.resolve(\(metatype(returnType)), for: \"\(member)\"\(fallback))")
            } else {
                w.line("return")
            }
        }
        let call = isThrowing ? "invokeThrowing" : "invoke"
        let prefix = (isThrowing ? "try " : "") + (isAsync ? "await " : "")
        w.line("return \(prefix)runtime.\(call)(\"\(identity)\", key: \(key)\(args))")
    }

    // MARK: Pieces

    /// Resolved D1: async members of a protocol without a global actor run on the caller's
    /// executor, so a `@MainActor` test's `when { … }` closure never hops before recording.
    private func nonsending(_ isAsync: Bool) -> String {
        isAsync && model.globalActor == nil ? "nonisolated(nonsending) " : ""
    }

    /// Methods: `_ name: T` / `label name: T` / `name: T`. Subscripts: `name: T` means no label.
    private func declaration(_ p: Parameter, subscriptStyle: Bool) -> String {
        switch p.label {
        case nil: return subscriptStyle ? "\(p.name): \(p.type)" : "_ \(p.name): \(p.type)"
        case p.name?: return subscriptStyle ? "\(p.name) \(p.name): \(p.type)" : "\(p.name): \(p.type)"
        case let label?: return "\(label) \(p.name): \(p.type)"
        }
    }

    private func keyList(genericTypes: [String], parameters: [Parameter]) -> String {
        let types = genericTypes.map { "arg(type: \($0).self)" }
        let values = parameters.filter { !$0.isClosure }.map { p in
            p.isMetatype ? "arg(type: \(p.name))" : "arg(\(p.name))"
        }
        return "[" + (types + values).joined(separator: ", ") + "]"
    }

    private func argsList(_ names: [String]) -> String {
        names.isEmpty ? "" : ", args: " + names.joined(separator: ", ")
    }
}

/// `(any P).self` and `(A, B).self` need parentheses; other types take `.self` directly.
func metatype(_ type: String) -> String {
    if type.hasPrefix("any ") || type.hasPrefix("some ") { return "(\(type)).self" }
    return "\(type).self"
}

private extension String {
    func indented() -> String {
        split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)
            .map { $0.isEmpty ? "" : "    " + $0 }.joined(separator: "\n")
    }
}
```

The body writer starts at indentation level 0. `indented()` shifts its output one level into the class body. The class `block` adds one more level per line it writes, so pass `body.output` through `lines(_:)` **without** `indented()` if the levels come out doubled. The snapshot test shows the first differing line; fix the emitter, not the golden.

`Sources/SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore/DummySynthesizer.swift` (minimal: structs only):

```swift
import SwiftSyntax

final class DummySynthesizer {
    let index: SourceIndex
    let model: MockModel
    private(set) var helpers: [String] = []
    private(set) var warnings: [GeneratorDiagnostic] = []
    private var built: Set<String> = []

    init(index: SourceIndex, model: MockModel) {
        self.index = index
        self.model = model
    }

    /// The `fallback:` argument for a type the runtime has no built-in for, or nil.
    /// `warn: false` is used for throwing members' placeholders: no dummy there only
    /// matters inside `verifyInOrder`, which reports it at runtime.
    func fallback(for type: String, member: String, genericNames: Set<String>, warn: Bool = true) -> String? {
        let t = type.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
        if BuiltIns.covers(t) { return nil }
        guard case .structDecl(let decl)? = index.typeDecl(named: t) else { return nil }
        let name = "_dummy\(t)"
        if built.insert(name).inserted {
            let arguments = storedProperties(decl.node).map {
                "\($0.name): Dummies.resolve(\(metatype($0.type)), for: \"\(t).\($0.name)\")"
            }
            helpers.append("private static func \(name)() -> \(t) {\n    \(t)(\(arguments.joined(separator: ", ")))\n}")
        }
        return "Self.\(name)"
    }

    /// Stored properties that the memberwise initializer takes, in declaration order.
    func storedProperties(_ decl: StructDeclSyntax) -> [(name: String, type: String)] {
        decl.memberBlock.members.compactMap { $0.decl.as(VariableDeclSyntax.self) }
            .filter { variable in !variable.modifiers.contains { $0.name.text == "static" } }
            .flatMap { variable in
                variable.bindings.compactMap { binding -> (name: String, type: String)? in
                    guard binding.accessorBlock == nil,
                          !(variable.bindingSpecifier.text == "let" && binding.initializer != nil),
                          let name = binding.pattern.as(IdentifierPatternSyntax.self)?.identifier.text,
                          let type = binding.typeAnnotation?.type.trimmedDescription else { return nil }
                    return (name, type)
                }
            }
    }
}

enum BuiltIns {
    static let names: Set<String> = [
        "Void", "()", "Bool", "String", "Character", "Data", "Date", "URL", "UUID",
        "Int", "Int8", "Int16", "Int32", "Int64", "UInt", "UInt8", "UInt16", "UInt32", "UInt64",
        "Double", "Float",
    ]

    /// Types the runtime's `Dummies.lookup` builds. `Result` is excluded on purpose:
    /// its dummy needs the success type's dummy, which the synthesizer handles.
    static func covers(_ type: String) -> Bool {
        if names.contains(type) || type.hasSuffix("?") || type.hasSuffix("!") { return true }
        return ["[", "Array<", "Set<", "Dictionary<", "Optional<"].contains { type.hasPrefix($0) }
    }
}
```

`Sources/SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore/Generator.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

public struct GeneratorConfiguration: Sendable {
    public var markedPaths: [String]
    public var inputs: [SourceInput]
    public var testModule: String
    public var outputDirectory: String
    public var expectedFiles: [String]

    public init(markedPaths: [String], inputs: [SourceInput], testModule: String,
                outputDirectory: String, expectedFiles: [String] = []) {
        self.markedPaths = markedPaths
        self.inputs = inputs
        self.testModule = testModule
        self.outputDirectory = outputDirectory
        self.expectedFiles = expectedFiles
    }
}

public struct GeneratorResult: Sendable {
    public let files: [String: String]
    public let diagnostics: [GeneratorDiagnostic]
    public var hasErrors: Bool { diagnostics.contains { $0.severity == .error } }
}

public enum Generator {
    public static func generate(_ configuration: GeneratorConfiguration) -> GeneratorResult {
        let index = SourceIndex(configuration.inputs)
        let resolver = ProtocolResolver(index: index)
        var files: [String: String] = [:]
        var diagnostics: [GeneratorDiagnostic] = []

        for marker in index.markers(in: Set(configuration.markedPaths)) {
            let fileName = "Mock\(marker.protocolName).swift"
            guard files[fileName] == nil else {
                diagnostics.append(.error("Mock\(marker.protocolName) is generated twice; remove the duplicate @GenerateMock(\(marker.protocolName).self)", at: marker))
                continue
            }
            switch resolver.resolve(marker, testModule: configuration.testModule) {
            case .success(let model):
                let synthesizer = DummySynthesizer(index: index, model: model)
                files[fileName] = MockEmitter(model: model, synthesizer: synthesizer).emit()
                diagnostics += synthesizer.warnings
            case .failure(let failure):
                diagnostics += failure.diagnostics
                let summary = failure.diagnostics.map(\.message).joined(separator: "; ").replacingOccurrences(of: "\"", with: "'")
                files[fileName] = "// Generated by SwiftMockito. Generation failed.\n#error(\"\(summary)\")\n"
            }
        }
        for expected in configuration.expectedFiles where files[expected] == nil {
            let name = expected.dropFirst("Mock".count).dropLast(".swift".count)
            files[expected] = "// Generated by SwiftMockito. No active @GenerateMock(\(name).self) found.\n"
        }
        return GeneratorResult(files: files, diagnostics: diagnostics)
    }

    /// CLI entry point. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 generation errors, 2 usage errors.
    public static func run(arguments: [String]) -> Int32 {
        guard arguments.first == "generate" else { return usageError() }
        var testModule: String?
        var output: String?
        var marked: [String] = []
        var sources: [(module: String, path: String)] = []
        var expected: [String] = []
        var remaining = arguments.dropFirst().makeIterator()
        while let flag = remaining.next() {
            guard let value = remaining.next() else { return usageError() }
            switch flag {
            case "--test-module": testModule = value
            case "--output": output = value
            case "--marked": marked.append(value)
            case "--expect": expected.append(value)
            case "--source", "--source-dir":
                guard let eq = value.firstIndex(of: "=") else { return usageError() }
                let module = String(value[..<eq])
                let path = String(value[value.index(after: eq)...])
                if flag == "--source" {
                    sources.append((module, path))
                } else {
                    sources += swiftFiles(in: path).map { (module, $0) }
                }
            default:
                return usageError()
            }
        }
        guard let testModule, let output else { return usageError() }

        func read(_ path: String) -> String { (try? String(contentsOfFile: path, encoding: .utf8)) ?? "" }
        var inputs = marked.map { SourceInput(path: $0, module: testModule, text: read($0)) }
        inputs += sources.filter { !marked.contains($0.path) }.map { SourceInput(path: $0.path, module: $0.module, text: read($0.path)) }

        let result = generate(GeneratorConfiguration(markedPaths: marked, inputs: inputs, testModule: testModule,
                                                     outputDirectory: output, expectedFiles: expected))
        try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: output, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
        for (name, contents) in result.files.sorted(by: { $0.key < $1.key }) {
            let path = (output as NSString).appendingPathComponent(name)
            if read(path) != contents {   // keep mtimes stable for incremental builds
                try? contents.write(toFile: path, atomically: true, encoding: .utf8)
            }
        }
        for diagnostic in result.diagnostics {
            FileHandle.standardError.write(Data((diagnostic.description + "\n").utf8))
        }
        return result.hasErrors ? 1 : 0
    }

    static let usage = """
        usage: SwiftMockitoGenerator generate --test-module <Module> --output <dir>
               --marked <file.swift>... [--source <Module>=<file.swift>...]
               [--source-dir <Module>=<dir>...] [--expect <MockName.swift>...]

        """

    private static func usageError() -> Int32 {
        FileHandle.standardError.write(Data(usage.utf8))
        return 2
    }

    /// Swift files under `directory`, excluding generated `Mock*.swift` files.
    private static func swiftFiles(in directory: String) -> [String] {
        let enumerator = FileManager.default.enumerator(atPath: directory)
        var result: [String] = []
        while let relative = enumerator?.nextObject() as? String {
            let name = (relative as NSString).lastPathComponent
            guard name.hasSuffix(".swift"), !name.hasPrefix("Mock") else { continue }
            result.append((directory as NSString).appendingPathComponent(relative))
        }
        return result.sorted()
    }
}
```

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: `DummySynthesizer.fallback(for:member:genericNames:warn:)`. It covers structs (an accessible init, or the memberwise init), enums (the first case, with payload dummies), classes (an accessible init), protocols and `any P` (a nested `_Dummy<P>` class whose members trap), tuples (an inline closure), and `Result<S, F>` (`.success` with `S`'s dummy). import Foundation

```swift
struct Profile: Equatable {

    let tags: [String]
```

```swift
// Generated by SwiftMockito from Store. Do not edit.
import Foundation
import SwiftMockito

final class MockStore: Mock, Store, @unchecked Sendable {
    init(fileID: String = #fileID, filePath: StaticString = #filePath, line: UInt = #line, column: UInt = #column) {
        super.init(name: "MockStore", site: CallSite(fileID: fileID, filePath: filePath, line: line, column: column))
    }

    func profile() -> Profile {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "profile()", key: [])
            return Dummies.resolve(Profile.self, for: "MockStore.profile()", fallback: Self._dummyProfile)
        }
        return runtime.invoke("profile()", key: [])
    }

    func status() -> Status {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "status()", key: [])
            return Dummies.resolve(Status.self, for: "MockStore.status()", fallback: Self._dummyStatus)
        }
        return runtime.invoke("status()", key: [])
    }

    func session() -> Session {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "session()", key: [])
            return Dummies.resolve(Session.self, for: "MockStore.session()", fallback: Self._dummySession)
        }
        return runtime.invoke("session()", key: [])
    }

    func logger() -> any Logger {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "logger()", key: [])
            return Dummies.resolve((any Logger).self, for: "MockStore.logger()", fallback: Self._dummyLogger)
        }
        return runtime.invoke("logger()", key: [])
    }

    func pair() -> (Int, String) {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "pair()", key: [])
            return Dummies.resolve((Int, String).self, for: "MockStore.pair()", fallback: { (Dummies.resolve(Int.self, for: "MockStore.pair().0"), Dummies.resolve(String.self, for: "MockStore.pair().1")) })
        }
        return runtime.invoke("pair()", key: [])
    }

    func result() -> Result<Profile, Error> {
        if let capture = Capture.current {
            capture.record(runtime, "result()", key: [])
            return Dummies.resolve(Result<Profile, Error>.self, for: "MockStore.result()", fallback: { .success(Self._dummyProfile()) })
        }
        return runtime.invoke("result()", key: [])
    }

    private static func _dummyProfile() -> Profile {
        Profile(user: Dummies.resolve(User.self, for: "Profile.user", fallback: Self._dummyUser), tags: Dummies.resolve([String].self, for: "Profile.tags"), score: Dummies.resolve(Double.self, for: "Profile.score"))
    }

    private static func _dummyUser() -> User {
        User(id: Dummies.resolve(String.self, for: "User.id"), name: Dummies.resolve(String.self, for: "User.name"))
    }

    private static func _dummyStatus() -> Status {
        .active(since: Dummies.resolve(Date.self, for: "Status.active.since"))
    }

    private static func _dummySession() -> Session {
        Session(id: Dummies.resolve(UUID.self, for: "Session.init.id"))
    }

    private static func _dummyLogger() -> any Logger {
        _DummyLogger()
    }

    private final class _DummyLogger: Logger, @unchecked Sendable {
        var level: Int { fatalError("SwiftMockito: dummy Logger.level must not be called") }
        func log(_ message: String) { fatalError("SwiftMockito: dummy Logger.log(_:) must not be called") }
    }
}
```

Helper order: each helper is appended when it is first requested, depth-first. Building `Profile` requests `User`, so `_dummyUser` follows `_dummyProfile`. A `_Dummy` class follows its `_dummy` function.

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement the synthesizer**

Replace `DummySynthesizer.fallback(for:member:genericNames:warn:)` with the full algorithm. Keep the signature. When `warn` is false, follow the same steps but record no warnings (used for throwing members' placeholders). `t` is the trimmed type string, and `member` is `"Mock<P>.<identity>"` (used in warnings). Warnings use `.warning(_:at: model.marker)` and are deduplicated per mock.

1. `BuiltIns.covers(t)` → return `nil` (the runtime has it). Keep Task 13's function-type case, which returns a trapping closure literal, before the steps below.
2. If `t` is in `genericNames`, warn "`<member>`: cannot build a dummy for generic return type `t`; call provideDummy(_:) for each concrete `t` you stub" and return `nil`.
3. Tuple `(A, B, …)`: parse with `TypeSyntax("\(raw: t)")` and check for a `TupleTypeSyntax` with more than one element. Return `{ (e0, e1, …) }`, where element `i` is `Dummies.resolve(<metatype(Ei)>, for: "<member>.<i>"<, fallback: F>)` with `F = fallback(for: Ei, …)`.
4. `Result<S, F>`: return `{ .success(<s>) }`. `<s>` is `<helperRef>()` when `fallback(for: S)` returns a `Self._dummyX` reference, and otherwise `Dummies.resolve(<metatype(S)>, for: "<member>.success")`.
5. `any P`, or a bare name found as `.protocolDecl`: add helper `private static func _dummyP() -> any P {\n    _DummyP()\n}` and the nested class `private final class _DummyP: P, @unchecked Sendable { … }`. Get the requirements from `ProtocolResolver(index:).members(of:marker:)`. Emit one line per requirement, using the same parameter-declaration rules as `MockEmitter` (move `declaration(_:subscriptStyle:)` to a shared free function). Methods get `func name(params) effects -> R { fatalError("SwiftMockito: dummy P.<identity> must not be called") }`. Get-only properties get `var name: T { fatalError(…) }`; settable ones get `var name: T { get { fatalError(…) } set { fatalError(…) } }`. Return `Self._dummyP`.
6. `.structDecl`: if there are explicit `init`s that are not `private`/`fileprivate`, take the one with the fewest parameters and use `for: "S.init.<label>"`. With no explicit `init`, use the memberwise initializer over the stored properties (as in Task 13) with `for: "S.<property>"`. If every explicit init is private, warn "no accessible initializer" and return `nil`.
7. `.enumDecl`: take the first element of the first `case` declaration. Keep payload labels (`.active(since: …)`); unlabeled payloads are positional. Use `for: "E.<case>.<label or index>"`. With no cases, warn "(enum has no cases)" and return `nil`.
8. `.classDecl`: use the accessible `init` with the fewest parameters (`for: "C.init.<label>"`). With no `init` where every stored property has an initial value, use `C()`. Otherwise warn "no accessible initializer" and return `nil`.
9. Anything else: warn "cannot build a dummy `t` (not declared in sources); call provideDummy(_:) with a `t` before stubbing or verifying it" and return `nil`.

Every argument expression calls `fallback(for:member:genericNames: [])` recursively for its own type, and appends `, fallback: <ref>` when that returns non-nil. Keep an `inProgress: Set<String>` stack. Meeting a type already in progress means a recursive type: warn "(recursive type)" for the **outermost** requested type and return `nil` for it. Recursion through `Optional` (`Node?`) is fine, because Optional is a built-in and never recurses. The warning wording is uniform: "`<member>`: cannot build a dummy `<t>` (`<reason>`); call provideDummy(_:) with a `<t>` before stubbing or verifying it".

```swift
import SwiftCompilerPlugin
import SwiftSyntax
import SwiftSyntaxMacros

/// A marker only. A macro cannot see the protocol's body, so the build plugin
/// reads `@GenerateMock(P.self)` from the source and generates `MockP`.
public struct GenerateMockMacro: PeerMacro {
    public static func expansion(
        of node: AttributeSyntax,
        providingPeersOf declaration: some DeclSyntaxProtocol,
        in context: some MacroExpansionContext
    ) throws -> [DeclSyntax] {
        []
    }
}

@main
struct SwiftMockitoMacrosPlugin: CompilerPlugin {
    let providingMacros: [Macro.Type] = [GenerateMockMacro.self]
}
```

`Sources/SwiftMockito/GenerateMock.swift`:

```swift
/// Marks protocols to mock. It expands to nothing: the SwiftMockito build plugin reads it
/// and generates `Mock<Protocol>` into the test target.
///
///     @GenerateMock(Client.self)
///     enum Mocks {}
@attached(peer)
public macro GenerateMock(_ protocols: Any.Type...) = #externalMacro(module: "SwiftMockitoMacros", type: "GenerateMockMacro")
```

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: the `.plugin(name: "SwiftMockitoPlugin", targets: ["SwiftMockitoPlugin"])` product, a build-tool plugin with a shared `commands(tool:workDirectory:testModule:marked:sources:) throws -> [Command]` function (reused by Task 17), and `public enum MarkerScanner { static func protocolNames(in text: String) -> [String] }`.

Why a text pre-scan: build commands must declare their outputs before they run, and `prebuildCommand` cannot use an executable built from source. The plugin passes every scanned name as `--expect`, and the generator always writes every expected file. A disagreement between the scanner and the parser, such as a marker inside a comment, therefore produces a harmless comment-only file, never a missing output.

The plugin passes the test target's own sources as `--marked`, plus the sources of every recursive source-module dependency except SwiftMockito and the dependencies that SwiftMockito pulls in (its macro target and swift-syntax). Those add thousands of files and no user protocols.

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement**

`Sources/SwiftMockitoGeneratorCore/MarkerScanner.swift` (copy it byte for byte to `Plugins/SwiftMockitoPlugin/MarkerScanner.swift`):

```swift
import Foundation

/// Finds `@GenerateMock(A.self, B.self)` names with a text scan. The plugin uses it to
/// declare outputs before the generator runs; the generator re-parses with SwiftSyntax.
public enum MarkerScanner {
    public static func protocolNames(in text: String) -> [String] {
        var names: [String] = []
        var rest = text[...]
        while let start = rest.range(of: "@GenerateMock(") {
            guard let end = rest[start.upperBound...].firstIndex(of: ")") else { break }
            for part in rest[start.upperBound..<end].split(separator: ",") {
                let trimmed = part.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
                if trimmed.hasSuffix(".self") { names.append(String(trimmed.dropLast(5))) }
            }
            rest = rest[end...]
        }
        return names
    }
}
```

`Plugins/SwiftMockitoPlugin/SwiftMockitoPlugin.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import PackagePlugin

@main
struct SwiftMockitoPlugin: BuildToolPlugin {
    func createBuildCommands(context: PluginContext, target: Target) async throws -> [Command] {
        guard let target = target as? SourceModuleTarget else { return [] }
        let dependencies = target.recursiveTargetDependencies.compactMap { $0 as? SourceModuleTarget }
        // SwiftMockito and everything it depends on (macros, swift-syntax) hold no user protocols.
        let runtime = dependencies.first { $0.moduleName == "SwiftMockito" }
        let excluded = Set(([runtime].compactMap { $0 } + (runtime?.recursiveTargetDependencies ?? [])).map(\.id))
        let sources = dependencies
            .filter { !excluded.contains($0.id) }
            .flatMap { dependency in dependency.sourceFiles(withSuffix: "swift").map { (dependency.moduleName, $0.url) } }
        return try commands(
            tool: context.tool(named: "SwiftMockitoGenerator").url,
            workDirectory: context.pluginWorkDirectoryURL,
            testModule: target.moduleName,
            marked: target.sourceFiles(withSuffix: "swift").map(\.url),
            sources: sources
        )
    }
}

func commands(tool: URL, workDirectory: URL, testModule: String, marked: [URL],
              sources: [(module: String, url: URL)]) throws -> [Command] {
    let names = Set(try marked.flatMap { MarkerScanner.protocolNames(in: try String(contentsOf: $0, encoding: .utf8)) }).sorted()
    guard !names.isEmpty else { return [] }
    let output = workDirectory.appending(path: "GeneratedMocks")
    var arguments = ["generate", "--test-module", testModule, "--output", output.path]
    for url in marked { arguments += ["--marked", url.path] }
    for (module, url) in sources { arguments += ["--source", "\(module)=\(url.path)"] }
    for name in names { arguments += ["--expect", "Mock\(name).swift"] }
    return [.buildCommand(
        displayName: "SwiftMockito: generating \(names.count) mock(s) for \(testModule)",
        executable: tool,
        arguments: arguments,
        inputFiles: marked + sources.map(\.url),
        outputFiles: names.map { output.appending(path: "Mock\($0).swift") }
    )]
}
```

Manifest: the target `.plugin(name: "SwiftMockitoPlugin", capability: .buildTool(), dependencies: ["SwiftMockitoGenerator"])` and the product `.plugin(name: "SwiftMockitoPlugin", targets: ["SwiftMockitoPlugin"])`.

### Task 17: Xcode project plugin and the checked-in-mocks workflow

**Files:**
- Modify: `Plugins/SwiftMockitoPlugin/SwiftMockitoPlugin.swift`
- Create: `IntegrationTests/CheckedInMocks/check.sh`
- Create: `docs/xcode-plugin-verification.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `commands(tool:workDirectory:testModule:marked:sources:)` from Task 16, and the generator CLI.
- Produces: `extension SwiftMockitoPlugin: XcodeBuildToolPlugin`, and a script that regenerates the goldens with the CLI and fails when they differ from the checked-in files.

- [ ] **Step 1: Implement the Xcode extension**

Append to `SwiftMockitoPlugin.swift`:

```swift
#if canImport(XcodeProjectPlugin)
import XcodeProjectPlugin

extension SwiftMockitoPlugin: XcodeBuildToolPlugin {
    /// Xcode does not expose target dependencies to plugins, so the plugin searches the
    /// Swift files of every other target in the project for the protocol and its types.
    func createBuildCommands(context: XcodePluginContext, target: XcodeTarget) throws -> [Command] {
        let sources = context.xcodeProject.targets
            .filter { $0.id != target.id }
            .flatMap { other in
                other.inputFiles.filter { $0.url.pathExtension == "swift" }.map { (moduleName(other), $0.url) }
            }
        return try commands(
            tool: context.tool(named: "SwiftMockitoGenerator").url,
            workDirectory: context.pluginWorkDirectoryURL,
            testModule: moduleName(target),
            marked: target.inputFiles.filter { $0.url.pathExtension == "swift" }.map(\.url),
            sources: sources
        )
    }

    private func moduleName(_ target: XcodeTarget) -> String {
        (target.product?.name ?? target.displayName)
            .replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "_")
            .replacingOccurrences(of: " ", with: "_")
    }
}
#endif
```

```markdown
# Verifying the Xcode plugin

`XcodeProjectPlugin` only exists inside Xcode. CI compiles it (`xcodebuild … build`) but cannot run it.

1. Create a new iOS App project "Demo" with a unit-test target "DemoTests".
2. File ▸ Add Package Dependencies ▸ Add Local… ▸ select this repository.
3. Under DemoTests ▸ Build Phases ▸ Run Build Tool Plug-ins, click + and add SwiftMockitoPlugin. Link SwiftMockito to DemoTests.
4. Add `protocol Client { func cached(id: String) -> String? }` to Demo. In DemoTests, add
   `@GenerateMock(Client.self) enum Mocks {}` and a test that uses `MockClient()`.
5. Press ⌘U. Expected: the build log shows "SwiftMockito: generating 1 mock(s) for DemoTests" and the test passes.
6. Rename `cached` to `cache` in Demo and build again. Expected: the mock regenerates and the test's old `cached` call fails to compile.
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Checked-in mocks script**

`IntegrationTests/CheckedInMocks/check.sh` is the CI path for teams that commit their generated mocks:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Regenerates the golden mocks with the CLI and fails if they differ from the checked-in files.
set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
out="$(mktemp -d)"
fixtures="$root/Tests/SwiftMockitoTests/Fixtures"
printf '@GenerateMock(Client.self, Catalog.self, Screen.self, Feed.self, Edge.self, Store.self, Shapes.self)\nenum Mocks {}\n' > "$out/Mocks.swift"
swift run --package-path "$root" SwiftMockitoGenerator generate \
  --test-module SwiftMockitoTests --output "$out/generated" --marked "$out/Mocks.swift" \
  --source-dir "SwiftMockitoTests=$fixtures"
for name in MockClient MockCatalog MockScreen MockFeed MockEdge MockStore MockShapes; do
  diff -u "$fixtures/$name.swift" "$out/generated/$name.swift"
done
echo "checked-in mocks are up to date"
```

`--source-dir` skips files whose first line is `// Generated by SwiftMockito` (Task 13's `swiftFiles`), so the goldens are not read back in as inputs.

Run: `bash IntegrationTests/CheckedInMocks/check.sh`
Expected: `checked-in mocks are up to date`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Public-API guard**

`Scripts/check-public-api.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Fails if the SwiftMockito module exports matcher-style symbols. The spec forbids them.
set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
swift package --package-path "$root" dump-symbol-graph --minimum-access-level public >/dev/null
graph=$(find "$root/.build" -path "*symbolgraph*" -name "SwiftMockito.symbols.json" | head -1)
[ -n "$graph" ] || { echo "symbol graph not found"; exit 1; }
names=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("\n".join(s["names"]["title"] for s in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["symbols"]))' "$graph")
forbidden='^(any|anyArg|argThat|captor|ArgumentCaptor|wildcard|isA|eq|predicate|matching)(\(|$)'
if echo "$names" | grep -E "$forbidden"; then
  echo "forbidden matcher symbol(s) in public API"
  exit 1
fi
echo "public API has no matcher symbols ($(echo "$names" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') symbols checked)"
```

Run: `bash Scripts/check-public-api.sh`
Expected: `public API has no matcher symbols (…)`.
